label: Wet Market Unique ID (system assigned)

label: Enumerator Name
hint: Enter the full name of the field enumerator.

label: Zonal Officer Name
hint: Example: Kranthi. Enter the name of the zonal officer associated with the assessment.

label: Date of Assessment
hint: Example format: 10/12/2026. Select the actual assessment date.

label: Time of Assessment (Start)
hint: Example: 6:30 AM. Record the actual start time.

label: Time of Assessment (End)
hint: Record the actual end time of this assessment.

label: GHMC Zone
hint: Select the GHMC zone. Circle and Ward options are filtered using this zone mapping.

label: Circle
hint: Only circles mapped to the selected old zone are shown.

label: Ward Number — Ward Name
hint: Select the ward matching the selected GHMC Zone and Circle. Choose Others if the ward is not listed.

label: Specify Other Ward Number and Name
hint: Enter the ward number and ward name.

label: Market Area Name
hint: Example: Ram Nagar Fish Market. Enter the market or market-area name.

label: Site / Shop Name
hint: Example: Mangamma Fish Retail Shop. Enter the actual shop/stall name.

label: Shop License Number (GHMC, if any)
hint: Example: GHMC/WET-1201-2026. Enter the displayed licence number, if available; otherwise leave blank.

label: Owner Name
hint: Example: Mangamma. Enter the actual owner name.

label: Owner Contact Number
hint: Example: 9177335507. Enter 10–15 digits only; leave blank if unavailable.

label: Lead / In-charge Name (Optional)
hint: Example: Laxmi. Optional; enter the person responsible for the shop/stall.

label: Lead / In-charge Contact Number (Optional)
hint: Example: 9177335507. Optional; enter digits only if available.

label: Shop Address
hint: Example: 1-10-203-1, Zamistanpur, Near More Market Road, RamNagar. Enter the full actual address and landmark.

label: Area of the Shop (sq. ft.)
hint: Example: 200sqft

label: GPS Coordinates (Latitude and Longitude)
hint: Capture the point at the assessed shop/stall, not only the market entrance. Example: 17.439354, 78.448109. Capture the actual location; do not copy example coordinates for another site.

label: Upload Geotagged Shop / Stall Photograph
hint: Upload a photograph of the actual shop/stall, preferably showing the main entrance. Example: Shop Main Entrance. Ensure device/app location tagging is enabled if a geotag is required.

Domain A remarks / evidence / action required
Domain A: Critical red flag identified?
Domain A: Immediate action / referral / responsible person / due date
B1. Are live animals present? (Observe all stalls/holding areas within the assessment unit.)
B2. Which live animal species are present? (Select all applicable.)
B3. Are dead animals/animal products present?
B4. Which dead animal species/products are present? (Select all applicable.)
B5. Are animals from different species held in the same enclosure? (Observe whether two or more species physically share one cage/pen.)
B6. Are animals from different batches/sources physically mixed? (ask whether animals from different arrivals/suppliers are held together without a visible source/batch distinction.)
B7. Are animals visibly showing signs of illness? (Look for obvious abnormal behaviour, weakness, respiratory signs, diarrhoea, discharge, skin lesions or other visible illness; do not diagnose.)
B8. Are unexplained animal injuries or deaths present/reported? (Observe dead animals and ask whether unusual deaths/injuries occurred; note number/species if Yes.)
B9. Is there a designated isolation area for sick/injured animals? (Ask to see the separate area; it should prevent contact with animals for sale.)
B10. Are dead-on-arrival/unexpectedly dead animals excluded from sale? (Ask what happens to such animals.)
B11. Are dead-on-arrival/unexpectedly dead animals reported/disposed off safely? (Ask of disposal route; no open sale or uncontrolled dumping.)

label: C2. Are holding cages/pens structurally intact? (Look for broken wire, sharp edges, gaps, damaged doors/floors or escape points.)
C3. Are holding cages/pens easy to clean? (Surfaces should be accessible for removal of faeces/urine and washable without hidden inaccessible areas.)
C4. Can animals move normally within the enclosure? (Observe normal movement for the species; record if movement is restricted by crowding or enclosure design.)
C5. Is drinking water accessible to live animals? (Observe a water source physically reachable by the animals.)
C6. Is feed accessible where required? (Observe feed availability and whether animals can reach it.)
C7. Is feed protected from faecal/urine contamination? (Observe whether feed is placed where animals cannot contaminate it with waste.)
C8. Is drinking water protected from faecal/urine contamination? (Observe container location and contamination.)
C9. Are live animals separated from carcasses? (Observe physical separation; direct contact/shared floor or cage = not separated.)
C10. Are live animals separated from food/? (Observe physical separation from meat, fish, produce and ready-to-eat food.)
C11. Are cages/pens suitable for the species? (Observe whether size/design permits normal posture and movement for the species being held.)
C12. Is the holding area protected from direct sun/heat? (Observe whether animals are exposed to direct sunlight/rays without shade.)
C13. Are cages/pens suitable for the species? (Observe whether size/design permits normal posture and movement for the species being held.)
C14. Are unsold live animals routinely held overnight? (V3: animals seen at closing and next opening OR vendor confirms routine holding beyond one trading day.)
C15. Is animal movement one-way from entry/holding to sale/slaughter? (Observe whether animals return through clean/customer areas or cross the same route repeatedly.)

F1. Does slaughter or dressing occur on site?
F2. Is slaughter carried out in a designated restricted area? (Observe whether the activity is confined to a defined area away from customers/clean food.)

F20. Are condemned materials disposed of safely? (Ask/observe disposal route; no sale or open dumping.)
F21. Is wash water prevented from cross-use between dirty and clean activities? (Observe/ask whether contaminated water is reused for clean handling.)

J1. Do workers wash hands after slaughter/dressing? (Observe or ask.)
J2. Do workers wash hands after waste handling? (Observe or ask.)
J3. Do workers wash hands before food handling/eating? (Observe or ask.)
J4. Are gloves used during tasks where hand contamination/exposure risk is present? (Observe active high-exposure work; do not treat gloves as required for every task.)

J10. Are visible cuts/wounds covered when present? (Use only when J9 = Yes; observe whether the wound is securely covered.)

J12. Is a post-exposure procedure available? (Ask what a worker should do after a cut, splash or other occupational exposure.)
